## Highlights

Zova 1.3.0 extends the plugin host for applications that link their extension
code directly: plugins can read graph edge payloads through the data service,
the C ABI accepts plugin descriptors that are already linked into the host
process, and migration can be given the same extension code as open. Storage
stays at format 12, so databases written by 1.2.0 open unchanged.

## What's changed

- Added `ZOVA_PLUGIN_GRAPH_EDGE_PAYLOADS_GET` to the plugin data service. A
  plugin passes a batch of edge keys and receives one row per key, in input
  order, with a found flag and the payload. Payload bytes count toward the
  request's byte budget.
- Added `ZOVA_PLUGIN_GRAPH_NEIGHBORS_KEYED` to the plugin data service. One
  request reads the adjacency of a batch of node keys, with a direction and an
  optional edge type, so a traversal no longer makes one call per node or maps
  keys back to node ids. Rows are grouped by input key and pages resume from
  the last row.
- Added `zova_database_create_with_plugins`, `zova_database_open_with_plugins`
  and `zova_database_open_for_extension_upgrade_with_plugins` to the C ABI.
  They take `zova_plugin_descriptor_v1` pointers linked into the host process,
  optionally together with trusted `.zovaext` bundle paths, and compose them
  with the bundled extensions. Linked descriptors need no bundle and no trust
  record; the caller already runs that code.
- Added `zova_database_migrate_with_extensions` to the C ABI. It migrates a
  database whose installed extensions are not bundled with Zova by accepting
  the same bundle paths and linked descriptors as open. Plain
  `zova_database_migrate` still refuses such a database and publishes nothing.
- Documented and tested that a plugin's read-only operations may query
  application tables in `main` through the query service.
- Added the raw declarations for the new functions and request structs to
  `zova-sys`. The safe Rust, Python, Go and JavaScript APIs are unchanged.

## Compatibility

- Package and C ABI identity are `1.3.0`. The C ABI change is additive; code
  built against 1.2.0 keeps working.
- Storage format remains 12. No migration is needed from 1.2.0. Formats 9, 10
  and 11 keep their documented explicit migration path to format 12.
  Downgrades are unsupported.
- The plugin ABI stays at v1. A plugin that uses
  `ZOVA_PLUGIN_GRAPH_EDGE_PAYLOADS_GET` or `ZOVA_PLUGIN_GRAPH_NEIGHBORS_KEYED`
  must declare `zova_abi_min` `1.3.0`; a 1.2.0 host rejects those operations
  as invalid.
- Existing 1.x ownership, ordering, error, and transaction guarantees remain in
  force.

## Installation and distribution

- Native packages use `1.3.0` across Cargo, PyPI, npm, and Go.
- Python publishes CPython 3.13 stable-ABI wheels tested on Python 3.13 and
  3.14; no Python source distribution is published.
- npm publishes `zova-js`, its native companion packages, and the experimental
  `zova-wasm` package.
- Go's module tag is `bindings/go/v1.3.0`.

## Known boundaries

A single edge payload larger than the 1 MiB data-service page budget cannot be
read through the plugin data service. Linked plugin descriptors and
extension-aware migration are available through the C ABI and Zig only; the
high-level bindings do not wrap them yet. Core vector search remains exact;
approximate search is available only through the experimental USearch reference
extension. Extension authoring beyond the documented common C ABI, the
reference extensions, and the separate browser WASM API remain experimental and
outside the stable native 1.x compatibility commitment.

**Full Changelog:** https://github.com/ata-sesli/zova/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0
